title: Full-app crash: collab externalize throws on a doc with undefined library (agent-triggerable)
description:
LIVE on jhead.github.io/dash. A user reported the in-app AI AGENT crashed the whole app (uncaught TypeError, app dead). HEAD investigated: 3e7c6449.

=== Minified stack (user) ===
TypeError: can't access property "items", e.library is undefined
  <- O1e <- externalize <- getDoc <- onLocalChange <- unsubscribeStore <- r <- r <- setCollabUndo

So collab is ATTACHED (setCollabUndo). A local store change fires the collab outbound subscription (onLocalChange) -> getDoc -> externalize -> reads library.items on a doc whose library is UNDEFINED -> uncaught TypeError -> whole app crashes (it throws inside the Yjs/store subscription callback, not a catchable handler).

=== JOB 1 — crash site (CONFIRMED, file:line) ===
packages/authoring-ui/src/collab/assetExternalize.ts:65
  export function externalizeAssets(doc, store) {
    ...
    const items = doc.library.items.map(...)   // <-- UNGUARDED: doc.library.items
This is 'O1e' in the minified stack. It is invoked by the collab adapter's outbound hook:
  packages/authoring-ui/src/store/collabAdapter.ts:51-54  getDoc: () => { const doc = store.getState().history.present; return assets ? assets.externalize(doc) : doc; }
The adapter's externalize() == externalizeAssets(). getDoc is called from the FlashCollabBinding's onLocalChange store subscription. When doc.library is undefined, .items throws.
REPRODUCED (vitest, scratch test, now removed): createDocument(); delete doc.library; externalizeAssets(doc, new AssetStore()) -> throws TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading items)' (V8 wording; Firefox/minified = 'can't access property items, e.library is undefined'). instanceof TypeError confirmed.
Note: internalizeAssets / hasUnresolvedAssets / referencedAssetHashes in the SAME file are equally unguarded (all do doc.library.items), but the outbound externalize is the one on the reported stack.

=== JOB 2 — root cause / trigger (what yields library=undefined; the AGENT angle) ===
PRIMARY TRIGGER (agent op): the agent tool 'doc_load'.
  - Schema: packages/agent-protocol/src/index.ts:135  DocLoadParamsSchema = z.object({ document: z.unknown() })  -- accepts ANY value, ZERO structural validation.
  - Handler: packages/authoring-ui/src/agent/registry.ts:683  doc_load({document}) { cb.pushDoc(document as FlashDocument); }  -- blind cast, no validation, pushes straight into history.present.
  - Store: pushDoc/replaceDoc (store/documentStore.ts) do NOT enforce any library invariant; they just store the reference.
So an agent calling doc_load with a JSON doc that omits 'library' (e.g. {id, scenes, properties}) makes history.present.library === undefined. With collab attached, the resulting store change fires onLocalChange -> getDoc -> externalize -> crash. doc_load IS in the live tool surface (agent-protocol index.ts:980, dispatched via dispatchAgentCommand).

ASYMMETRY (why only outbound crashes): the collab INBOUND path is ALREADY fully defended:
  - schema.ts:994 rebuildDoc -> out.library = ylib instanceof Y.Map ? rebuildLibrary(ylib) : { items: [], folders: [] }
  - validate.ts:476 validateInboundDoc -> out.library = validateLibrary(raw.library) (total function, always returns {items,folders}).
A peer-produced doc therefore never lands library-less. Only the LOCAL outbound path (externalizeAssets) trusts the doc and is unguarded. (createDocument() always sets library via createLibrary() = {items:[],folders:[]}, so the normal solo path is safe.)
Other candidate paths that could also leave library undefined (not the reported one, but same class): any future mutation/handler that rebuilds a partial doc, a malformed FLA import, project restore. doc_load is the concrete proven trigger.

=== JOB 3 — two-sided fix direction ===
(a) ENFORCE library-present invariant at the doc-replacement boundary so the op cannot produce a library-less doc:
   - doc_load must NOT push an unvalidated doc. Validate/normalize the inbound document (reuse @flash/collab validateInboundDoc, which already coerces library = validateLibrary(raw.library) and scenes/properties) before pushDoc -- OR at minimum default library to {items:[],folders:[]} when absent. Tighten DocLoadParamsSchema beyond z.unknown(). Consider hardening pushDoc/replaceDoc to guarantee library is present (defense at the store boundary covers all current + future producers).
(b) DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH: externalizeAssets (and internalizeAssets/hasUnresolvedAssets/referencedAssetHashes) must GUARD against an undefined/empty library -- treat a missing library as an empty one (const items = doc.library?.items ?? []; return doc unchanged if no items) and NEVER throw. A buggy/agent/peer-produced doc must DEGRADE, not take down the whole app -- especially since this path is both agent- and collab-reachable and runs inside an uncatchable subscription callback. The collab adapter's getDoc could also try/catch the externalize and fall back to the raw doc.

ONE-LINE ROOT CAUSE: doc_load (agent tool, document: z.unknown(), blind cast + pushDoc) admits a doc with no library into history.present; the unguarded collab outbound externalizeAssets then does doc.library.items inside the onLocalChange subscription, throwing an uncaught TypeError that crashes the whole app. Fix both sides: validate/normalize doc_load input (library-present invariant) AND make externalize degrade gracefully on a library-less doc.
